note: Judged against the criteria as written, not against the fact that he bought thirty minutes later. MISSES: 'successful' — he works full-time in a hospital at 68 and the rep never asked what the role is, so the profile cannot be matched to 'business owner, physician or equivalent'; what is established is that he still has to work. 'Income' — decisively absent: 'making sure I have financial wherewithal to be able to retire comfortably. And I do not have that right now, so I can't retire', reinforced on the paired continuation call by $12,000 of air conditioning and a $17,000 solar commitment leaving no cash flow. 'Good_to_great' — five years of near-total training inactivity, progressive loss of glute and leg mass, bilateral knee problems, an ankle reconstruction and a cervical fusion; this is restoration and preservation, not an upgrade from good. MATCHES: 'neglected_health' — genuinely apt, he describes himself as being in good health and simply having let training slide under work pressure. 'Not_deconditioned' — he walks 8,500 to 11,000 steps daily, does yoga and calisthenics most mornings and has a lifetime of athletic history, so he is nothing like the excluded gym-averse profile. Scored 'outside' on three of five. THE FINDING: this prospect closed at full contract value on the immediately following call, which makes him the second clear case in the corpus — after Robyn Stillwater — of an out-of-ICP prospect converting at full price. He is also the first strong instance of the_preserver avatar, and the pattern that avatar predicts held exactly: no resistance to the value, real resistance to the liquidity, resolved instantly by moving the payment in time rather than by discounting. Taken with the two core-fit optimizers in this same batch who did not buy, the evidence is now pointing the same way from both directions: the stated ICP is not predicting purchase, and 'makes good money' in particular is screening on liquidity that the in-house payment plan already solves.
